name: PR Prep
description: Bundles the PR-handoff pair into one module: a configurable pre-PR quality-gate checklist that sweeps for unintended changes, secrets, dead code, and reviewer-flagged patterns, followed by an editable PR description generator that is plain-language, double-dash-free, and ticket-aware when ticket-work mode is active. Includes default-reviewer configuration for Bitbucket PRs.

checks.label: Checks
checks.description: User-managed list of pre-PR checks. Each entry is a check name plus a one-line description of what TPM should look for. Add or remove checks per project to match what your team's automated reviewer flags. The agent runs every enabled check in order and reports findings to the user before the PR is created.

Tests pass locally.value: Confirm with the user that they have run the project test suite and it passed. Do not assume; ask if uncertain.

No unintended file changes.value: Inspect git diff --name-only and confirm every modified file is genuinely part of the work. Flag anything that looks like it leaked from a prior task or local-only configuration.

No secrets or connection strings modifie.value: Scan diffs of appsettings.json, .env files, and config files for credential changes. Flag any token, key, password, or connection string edit.

No commented-out code left behind.value: Search the diff for blocks of commented-out code introduced this session. Old code should be deleted, not commented out.

No TODO or FIXME without a follow-up tic.value: Find new TODO or FIXME markers in the diff. Each one needs a linked ticket id or rationale, otherwise it's tech debt with no owner.

Error handling covers new code paths.value: Walk the new code paths and identify thrown errors, network calls, file I/O, and async boundaries. Confirm each has appropriate handling.

Null checks in place where needed.value: Identify nullable inputs to new code (function params, API responses, optional fields) and confirm they are checked before access.

No unused imports or dead code introduce.value: Scan for imports that aren't referenced and functions or variables that aren't used. Build warnings are usually a hint; do not rely on them alone.

Code follows existing naming conventions.value: Compare new identifiers (variables, functions, classes) against the project's existing naming patterns. Flag inconsistencies.

Edge cases addressed or documented.value: Recall the edge cases discussed during the session (or surfaced in QA findings). Each one should be either fixed in the diff or explicitly documented as out-of-scope.

Known reviewer patterns pre-empted.value: When tool.reviewer-dossier is loaded, check the diff against the project's reviewer dossier (patterns specific reviewers reliably flag) and confirm each pattern that applies here is addressed or deliberately left as-is. Treat this check as trivially passed when the dossier module is not loaded.

runMode.label: Run Mode
runMode.description: Controls how TPM presents the checklist. Interactive walks through each check one at a time and asks for user confirmation before moving on, useful for cases where the user wants to review each finding. Batched runs all checks at once and presents a single summary with all findings grouped together, faster but requires more context-switching to address issues. Allowed values: interactive or batched.

checklistAutoOffer.label: Checklist Auto-Offer
checklistAutoOffer.description: When on, TPM proactively offers to run the pre-PR checklist when the user signals they're done or ready to PR (ready for PR, let's wrap up, create a PR). When off, TPM only runs the checklist when the user explicitly asks for it. On is the typical flow for ticket-work sessions where the checklist is the first step of the PR-handoff ritual.

descriptionTemplate.label: PR Description Template
descriptionTemplate.description: Template for the PR description. TPM generates a draft here based on the session's work, then the operator edits it directly before submission. Supports markdown. The template is pre-filled when TPM drafts a description; edit it freely -- what you see is what gets submitted.
descriptionTemplate.default:
Change Summary:
[CHANGE SUMMARY - THREE SENTENCES MAXIMUM]

Verification: [LINK TO TESTING PROCS]

Has the UI been signed off by PO or manager? [ANSWER]

bannedTokens.label: Banned Tokens
bannedTokens.description: Comma-separated list of token sequences that must NEVER appear in the generated description. The default forbids ASCII double-dashes (which CodeRabbit flags), em-dash-with-hyphen-prefix, and the common '-- ' misuse. The agent scans every draft for these tokens and rewrites them before presenting the result to the user.

defaultReviewers.label: Default Reviewers
defaultReviewers.description: Reviewers to add to every PR. Each entry is a display name plus a Bitbucket account ID. Use the reviewer search in the PR Prep panel to find and add reviewers, or enter them manually. These are added by default; additional reviewers can be selected per-PR.
